transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you’re here. What brings you in today?
For about two months now, I've had this constant, terrifying feeling that people are watching and monitoring me, and I've also been hearing strange voices. It's left me feeling completely exhausted
During these two months, have you also had a period of feeling unusually energized or euphoric, needing much less sleep, or feeling much more talkative or impulsive than usual?
No, I haven't felt that way at all. If anything, I've just felt completely drained, exhausted, and down. I certainly haven't had any extra energy or felt happy.
Have you been feeling depressed or losing interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, during these same two months, or did the voices and feeling watched start before the low mood?

The voices and the feeling of being watched definitely started first, about two months ago. The depressed mood and losing interest in everything didn't set in until about a month ago. So those scary experiences were happening for a while before I started feeling so down.
Have the voices or feeling watched ever continued for at least two weeks when you were not feeling depressed or losing interest in things?

Yes, they have. For about a month before I started feeling really depressed and empty, I was hearing the voices and feeling monitored every single day. Even during that time when my mood was still normal, those experiences never stopped.
Have you had any major problems with work, school, relationships, self-care, or daily functioning since these symptoms started?

Yes, it has been incredibly difficult to manage anything lately. I've completely lost the motivation to do my work, and I feel too exhausted and drained of energy to handle basic daily tasks. I've also stopped talking to my friends and family because I just don't have the strength to interact with anyone anymore.
Based on the interview so far, the most likely diagnosis is Schizophrenia.

That diagnosis is a bit confusing to me because the severe sadness, emptiness, and lack of energy have actually been present for the majority of the entire two years I've been feeling sick. I still have those scary voices and feelings of being watched, but the constant depression has been the heaviest part of this whole experience. Are those long-term depressive feelings also factored into this diagnosis?
Have the depression and low energy been present for most of the time you’ve been ill, including when the voices or feeling watched were still happening?

Yes, they have. For most of the last two years, the depression and complete lack of energy have been there constantly, right alongside the voices and the feeling of being watched. They definitely happen at the same time, making it feel like I'm dealing with both of these heavy burdens at once.
Based on the interview so far, the most likely diagnosis is Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type).

Hearing that diagnosis is a bit scary, but it's also a relief to finally have a name for what I've been going through. It makes a lot of sense to me, since the severe depression and those terrifying voices have been overlapping for over two years now. I'm just really hoping we can find a way to treat both sides of this.
Based on the interview so far, the most likely diagnosis is Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type).

Yes, that diagnosis makes a lot of sense given how the depression and the voices have been overlapping for so long. What does this mean for my treatment plan going forward? I'm really hoping there is a way to help me manage both of these things.
